points.description: States that the compiler creates/inserts a copy of the inline function's code (the function body) — i.e., the function code is duplicated/expanded. Accept equivalent wording such as 'copies the function code' or 'places the function body in the program'.
points.partial_credit: If the answer says only that the function body/code is used/inserted but does not make clear that a copy is created, award part marks.

levels.says: Mentions that the function code/body is inserted or expanded at the call, but does not clearly state that a copy of the code is created.

points.description: States that this copy is made at every place/site where the function is called (each call location). Accept 'at each call', 'wherever the function is called', or equivalent.
points.partial_credit: If the answer mentions only a call site/location but not that it applies to every/each call, award part marks.

levels.says: Mentions the place of the function call but does not state that a copy is made at every/each call site.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both ideas: the compiler creates a copy of the function code and does this at every call site. Award part marks when only one idea is present or when the answer is vague about copying or about every call site. No marks for answers that do not mention copying/inserting the function code at call locations.
